chapter: Chicago clubs, entertainers and tent shows
title: Chicago dance and comedy acts: Butterbeans and Susie, Brown and McGraw
summary: Butterbeans and Susie were nightclub headliners in Chicago whose act Cheatham played many times. Louis Armstrong made the acrobatic husband-and-wife dancers Brown and McGraw famous by playing their whole act; later trumpeters were exhausted by it.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Did comedians also perform in the clubs, like at Dreamland --
Oh, yes, comedians performed in the clubs there.
What about the people like Butterbeans and Susie?
Well, Butterbeans he -- yes, they did a lot of night club work in Chicago, they were very popular, too. They were headliners. Butterbeans and Susie.
Uh-huh.
Yes, I played their act so many, many
times. And another famous act by the name of Brown and McGraw. Did you ever hear of them?
No.

They had a dance act, very fast dance act and I think their act lasted almost an hour. They also couldn't -- their act depended on the help of a trumpet player. Louie Armstrong was the first one to play that act. And Louie, in fact, made Brown and McGraw famous because their act was nothing without a trumpet. He blew them to death. Louie played to death for that act. Everything they did, Louie Armstrong was right on with the trumpet. So, after that, when they went out without Louie they had to have a trumpet player that could play. I mean when you got through with Brown and McGraw you were ready to go to the hospital, cause they would kill you.
They had everything written out.
This is Browning and McGraw?
Brown and McGraw.
Brown and McGraw.
Two people, man and wife. And they're very fast dance act. All was done with a trumpet player. So you had to go on the stage and play with them.
And what sort of dance would they do?
Well, it was a fast, dance like it was I think it was before the jitterbug.
Was it acrobatic?
Acrobatic and jazz. Oh, acrobatic, yes.
Was it something like the -- Nicholas Brothers?
Charleston and the tap and everything yes, all combined.
The splits?
The splits and everything, throw her all around and very fast type of dance act. But they depended on the trumpet. Trumpet player, very important part of that act.
Now of course there were no P.A. systems in those days.
No P.A. systems. They didn't need it because the acoustics of the theater were good enough, I think in those days.
